column3: Recurrent malignant salivary tumour: surgical excision with neck dissection, then adjuvant (chemo)radiotherapy; chemotherapy alone has a limited role.
Injury to the marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve during submandibular gland excision
An asymmetric smile after submandibular gland surgery is weakness of depressor anguli oris from injury to the marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve.

A 22-year-old man has a 2-cm thyroid nodule. His family history includes thyroid carcinoma and an unknown abdominal tumour in his father, now deceased; his BP is 145/90 mmHg. Fine-needle aspiration shows medullary thyroid carcinoma. Screening for which of the following must be undertaken before treatment of the thyroid carcinoma?
Familial medullary carcinoma suggests MEN2: exclude phaeochromocytoma (plasma metanephrines) first, as an unrecognised tumour can cause a fatal crisis at thyroidectomy.
In differentiated thyroid cancer, age is the strongest prognostic factor (AJCC 8th: ≥55 years is high risk); a 1-cm node-negative tumour otherwise has an excellent outlook.
